critical_interpretation_rules: Comparison across all four providers is a unified DISPLAY TABLE, not a unified controlled experiment. Arvan observations are from August 12/13, Sotoon-Kubit from September 27; different conditions and infrastructure states. Filter by run_id for valid within-session rankings.
Use original source pages and status notes. Do not calculate global overall provider winners from these rows.
Beware size, concurrency, duration, object counts, request batching, endpoint/tier, topology, network path, and time of day.

Latency percentiles printed by Warp text summaries were found to be biased unless --full/raw traces reaggregated. Report section 9.5 says section 5-8 earlier figures remain original, and Arvan LIST p50 is significantly corrected (~575 instead of 3243 ms); do not treat metrics as perfectly uniform.
Sotoon test used archive-labelled endpoint and purported cold bucket, apparently behaved as standard S3 interface; comparability of storage tier unconfirmed.
Arvan had an account access restriction for later live retesting; Arvan compatibility matrix is incomplete.
Some report statements are hypotheses about backend implementation (Ceph/SeaweedFS), not independently verified provider disclosures.

Benchmark report contains numeric observations, narrative diagnostic points, and suggested tests; this dataset covers tabulated comparison measurements and selected explicit diagnostics, not every numerical observation in prose.
When provider is 'Hamravesh HS3 (direct)' or 'Hamravesh HS3 (via proxy)', these are the same provider from a network-only experiment and must not count as extra providers.
open_review_items: The metric vocabulary mixes base metrics with run-level aggregates and one-off diagnostics: 28 labels, of which 67 rows use names such as throughput_run_min, list_empty_bucket_latency_p50_low or put_latency_p99_64kib. Normalize to a controlled vocabulary before ingestion.
Six rows have an empty object_size, and aggregation has nine distinct values; both need a defined schema before they can be observation identity keys.
Capability statuses for Arvan are mostly not_tested or blocked_by_account. Render them as unknown, never as unsupported.
derived/four_provider_overview.csv must be regenerated from observations.csv; a consistency test should guard against drift.
ingestion_guidance: Validate (run_id,provider,workload,metric,object_size,aggregation) as an observation identity, but repeated one-off diagnostics may require an observation_sequence key; preserve source_pdf_page. Store methodology JSON by run ID; show warnings on panel.
